title: Ops Synthesis & On-call Handover — 2026-06-04
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the SRE weekly synthesis: incidents, SLO health snapshot, on-call handoff notes, mitigations in flight, and prioritized action items. Intended audience: SREs, platform-engineering, release-engineering, and product incident stakeholders.

Attendees / contributors:
- Asha Iyer (owner, ops lead)
- Michael Chen (on-call primary, infra)
- Lena Ortiz (observability)
- Tomás Rivera (serving-runtime)
- Priya Nandakumar (release engineering)

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Two customer-impact incidents this week; a routing misconfiguration causing elevated p99 for dedicated pools (INC-2026-051) and a brief KV cache corruption after the 2026-06-02 runtime patch leading to transient 5xxs (INC-2026-052).
- Error budget burn accelerated for Dedicated model endpoints (10% budget used this week on high-priority routes).
- Short-term mitigations deployed; long-term fixes assigned with owners and tentative ETA.
- On-call handover notes and new runbook edits included below.

INCIDENTS (detailed):
1) INC-2026-051 — routing mismatch for dedicated pools (Severity: Sev2)
- Window: 2026-06-02 03:30–05:10 UTC
- Symptoms: sustained p99 token latency increase on dedicated inference pools in us-west-2 (~2.1–2.8s -> 6.4–8.0s). Error rate spiked for routes pinned to gtx-rt variants.
- Detection: alert from APM p99 > 3s for > 5m; repeat customer complaint (dedicated) escalated to SRE.
- Root cause hypothesis: a release in routing policy (rollout id: rollout-2026-06-01-3) unintentionally prefixed a low-priority routing rule so requests for dedicated customers were routed to burst nodes with different scheduling/eviction behavior.
- Immediate mitigation: rolled back rollout-2026-06-01-3 at 03:54 UTC; manual routing override applied to pin affected customers to their prior pool configuration. Latency returned to baseline by 05:10 UTC.
- Post-incident notes: review of rollout gating needed; add integration test that compares routing policy outputs for pinned customers.

2) INC-2026-052 — KV cache corruption after runtime patch (Severity: Sev3)
- Window: 2026-06-03 18:12–18:37 UTC
- Symptoms: transient 5xx errors (predominantly 502/504) on hosted-api model-variants using KV cache; smaller latency regressions for long-context requests.
- Detection: synthetic tests failing for long-context sequences; internal ping tests flagged increased error rate.
- Root cause: a corner-case in cache rehydration path introduced by runtime hotfix 2026.6.02.1 — under specific sequence lengths the KV index pointer could become stale after multi-host routing.
- Immediate mitigation: disabled the aggressive rehydration path and reverted to stable rehydration algorithm at 18:22 UTC; synthetic passing by 18:35 UTC.
- Follow-up: add fuzzing tests for sequence-length edge cases and strengthen canary coverage for multi-host rehydration.

SLO / Error budget snapshot (weekly):
- Platform-level request availability SLO (P99 success): target 99.95% monthly.
- Current month-to-date: 99.91% -> remaining error budget: ~67% (note: incidents this week consumed ~0.9% of budget).
- Dedicated-pools critical-route SLO: target 99.97% monthly; MTD: 99.89% -> remaining error budget: ~36%. Action: Notify account execs for customers nearing contract thresholds; engage CS for high-visibility customers.

Observability notes:
- Observability gaps surfaced: lack of end-to-end routing telemetry at the per-customer level. Current logs show final pool assignment but not routing decision diffs.
- Workaround: added a temporary trace tag in routing service to surface the applied rule id for the next 72 hours.
- Metric anomalies: KV cache hit rate dip correlated with 502 spikes; correlate with host churn metrics.

On-call handoff (current -> next):
- Outgoing on-call: Michael Chen (primary), handover at 2026-06-04 09:00 UTC.
- Incoming on-call: Priya Nandakumar (primary) for 2026-06-04 -> 2026-06-11. Backup: Tomás Rivera.
- Open alerts to watch (keys):
  - APM p99 latency > 3s for >5m on any dedicated pool
  - Synthetic long-context failure rate > 1% sustained for 10m
  - Error budget burn rate > 5% in a 7-day rolling window
- Current runbook updates:
  - Routing rollback checklist expanded (added commands to query rollout assignments and quick-apply override).
  - KV rehydration checklist: steps to trigger safe-rehydration and toggle rehydration throttle via feature-flag.

Action items (owner — due):
- Add routing policy unit test & integration test that simulates pinned-customer scenarios (Owner: Priya N., due: 2026-06-14).
- Implement end-to-end per-customer routing telemetry (Owner: Lena O., due: 2026-06-21).
- Expand canary tests for KV rehydration path; add multi-host fuzzing harness (Owner: Tomás R., due: 2026-06-18).
- Customer communications: CS to send impact summaries to affected accounts and provide mitigation timeline (Owner: Sarah K. (CS), due: 2026-06-06).
- Runbook edits: merge small runbook PRs and publish (Owner: Michael C., due: 2026-06-08).

Notes to self / informal items (scratchpad):
- Consider per-customer synthetic checks that run across both hosted and dedicated routing paths (cheap, hourly).
- Discuss quota/exemptions model for critical traffic in routing engine — maybe a priority-sla flag.
- Re-evaluate rollout gating thresholds — reduce simultaneous rollout % for routing service to 10% until routing telemetry improved.

Risks / open questions:
- Is there any customer-side config that could have amplified the routing mismatch (e.g., customers with explicit pinned tags)? Next step: query config database for affected customer set entries.
- Do we need a circuit-breaker at the scheduling layer to avoid overloading burst nodes when misrouted?

Follow-ups scheduled:
- Postmortem working session (internal) booked for 2026-06-09 16:00 UTC to go over INC-2026-051 and finalize postmortem draft.
- Observability design sync scheduled with product telemetry on 2026-06-11 10:00 UTC.

Appendix (quick links):
- INC-2026-051 incident page: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SRE/INC-2026-051
- KV rehydration PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482
- Runbook PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/99

End of doc.
